detail.title: An Investigation of Factors Impacting Job Stress-Related Presenteeism among Child Welfare Workers
detail.abstract: Presenteeism occurs when workers are physically present at work but functionally absent, thereby lowering the productivity and performance of workers, which impacts service delivery. While much is known about how illness-related presenteeism diminishes worker productivity, performance, and well-being; far less attention has been given to presenteeism driven by job stress—particularly within the child welfare workforce. This study used the Job Demands-Resources model to examine the impact of organizational factors on job stress-related presenteeism amongst frontline child welfare workers (N=733). A three-level hierarchical regression suggested that younger workers, role challenges, organizational characteristics, and job importance significantly predicted job stress-related presenteeism. A post-hoc investigation of role challenges and organizational characteristics revealed that organizational support reduced job stress-related presenteeism, whereas role conflict contributed to its increase. There is a need to offer support and implement mechanisms to reduce presenteeism and to further investigate job stress-related presenteeism among child welfare workers.

detail.title: Welfare After the End of Welfare Program

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by Peking University School of Economics Research Seed Grant, the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities, Peking University (No. 7100604836), and National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 72403011, 72203004, 72573006).

detail.abstract: Governments worldwide have implemented various means-tested programs to tackle poverty and deprivation, with mounting evidence on benefits when these programs are active. However, less is known about the post-program welfare dynamics. We study the exit of China's flagship anti-poverty program in 2021. Exploiting a discontinuity in the probability of selecting exited counties into continued assistance, we document an (unexpected) improvement in households' subjective well-being after the exit, with no evidence of economic decline. Material and emotional support from family and social networks rose to substitute for the withdrawing government assistance, explaining the rise in post-exit welfare. We highlight the role of social support in sustaining welfare after public aid cessation.

detail.title: Crypto-asset ownership among Spanish households

keywords: Survey of Financial Competences JEL classification D14

publicationDetails.journalName: Banco de Espana Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Rationale Crypto-assets have become an important economic and social phenomenon, associated with new ways of managing savings and investment. This article analyses their degree of penetration in Spain, the characteristics of their holders and their share in households' financial wealth. Takeaways • Spanish households' direct exposure to crypto-assets is limited. 4.8% of the Spanish population owned crypto-assets in 2021. For 80% of households owning crypto-assets, the share of these products in their financial portfolio did not exceed 10% in 2022. • Crypto-asset ownership is more prevalent among young men with a higher level of education and greater financial literacy. Crypto-asset holders consider themselves risk-tolerant, claim to plan their personal finances and also invest in other assets, such as shares and investment funds. They do not show any signs of rejecting the traditional financial system. • 0.6% of households hold a substantial portion of their wealth in crypto-assets, which entails greater exposure to the risks associated with these assets.

detail.abstract: The increasing digitalisation of means of payment is having a significant impact on how consumers pay. Analysing how means of payment are used allows us to assess whether consumers have safe, efficient and inclusive payment options available to them. Takeaways • The use of mobile devices at the point of sale has doubled since 2022, although cash and cards remain the most frequently used means of payment. • Cards are the chief payment method online and instant payments stand out in person-to-person payments. • The main factors persuading consumers to try out new means of payment are ease of use and higher security standards.

title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Supply Chain Disruptions: Firm-Level Evidence from "Liberation Day"

detail.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Supply Chain Disruptions: Firm-Level Evidence from "Liberation Day"
detail.abstract: On April 2, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump announced the “Liberation Day” tariffs, creating an unexpected, precisely timed, and country-specific episode of trade policy uncertainty. The proposal threatened U.S. trade partners with additional tariffs ranging from 10% to 50%, depending on the outcome of bilateral negotiations. Using transaction-level U.S. import data, we find that firms rapidly shifted sourcing from countries facing high tariff risk to those facing low tariff risk. Firms didn’t change their total import values but this reallocation came at the cost of higher import prices. Firms with relationship-sticky, contract-dependent, and trade finance-intensive supply chains drove this preemptive reallocation, consistent with their high vulnerability had tariffs taken effect before they could adjust. Our findings demonstrate that even brief periods of trade policy uncertainty can significantly disrupt supply chains.

AI.tldr: 本文研究了特朗普宣布'解放日'关税政策引发的贸易政策不确定性对供应链的影响。研究发现企业会迅速将采购从高关税风险国家转向低风险国家，这种重新配置导致进口价格上涨，但总进口值不变。关系粘性、合同依赖和贸易融资密集型企业是这种预防性重新配置的主要驱动者。

title: Transferable Development Rights and the Urban-Rural Income Divide: Evidence from China's Land Coupon Program
affiliations: , University of California, Davis - Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics and Renmin University of China

detail.title: Transferable Development Rights and the Urban-Rural Income Divide: Evidence from China's Land Coupon Program
detail.abstract: Inefficient land allocation between rural and urban areas remains a structural challenge in China, reinforced by rigid land-use regulations, the "land balance" policy, and sustained rural outmigration. To address these tensions, the central government in 2008 authorized Chongqing, a directly administered municipality, to pilot the Land Coupon Program (LCP), a market-based mechanism similar to transferable development rights, allowing rural construction quotas to be traded for urban expansion. This paper examines whether the LCP reduced the urban-rural income divide and through what channels. More broadly, it considers how government-led but market-based reforms can mitigate entrenched spatial disparities. Our study applies a recently developed approach, the model-averaging Matching and Synthetic Control estimator, at the provincial level and complementary county-level analyses. We show that the LCP lowered Chongqing's urban-rural income ratio by 0.3-0.4 between 2008 and 2019, accounting for about 40% of the overall decline. County-level results reveal that most convergence occurred within counties, driven by cumulative rather than annual transactions, with disadvantaged and fiscally capable areas participating earlier and trading more intensively. Beyond direct transfers, multiplier analysis suggests that the infusion of land-coupon revenues into rural households and collectives amplified local economic impacts. Our findings demonstrate that the LCP reduced inequality in a progressive and self-reinforcing manner, in contrast to earlier evidence that emphasized efficiency effects of land-use reforms. Our results highlight the broader potential of carefully designed, government-facilitated market mechanisms to promote inclusive growth and reduce spatial inequality in emerging economies despite institutional limitations on property rights and land transfers.

title: Was Well-being Gains Driven by China’s Energy Transition Strategies?

detail.title: Was Well-being Gains Driven by China’s Energy Transition Strategies?
detail.abstract: While China's accelerated energy transition has successfully decoupled macroeconomic growth from energy consumption, our analysis uncovers a counterproductive dynamic: the rise of a "service-locked" metabolic pattern. This pattern acts as a key intermediary, translating production-side efficiency gains into rigid, high-energy consumption lifestyles at the household level, without due consideration of societal costs. Consequently, household energy metabolism has accelerated, outpacing the growth of the service sector itself since 2015. Structural decomposition analysis confirms that resource and technology aggregation has become the dominant driver, overwhelming efforts toward structural mitigation. Thus, while this high-energy lifestyle enhances material energy well-being, it does so at the expense of temporal welfare. Provincial data further reveal a nationwide convergence toward this unbalanced energy-oriented well-being pathway, which exacerbates regional disparities. China's experience underscores that a truly sustainable and equitable global energy transition must be designed to integrally couple household energy demand with both energy security and temporal welfare.

AI.tldr: 中国能源转型虽然成功实现了经济增长与能源消费的脱钩，但却催生了"服务锁定"的代谢模式，导致家庭层面的高能耗生活方式，牺牲了时间福利并加剧了区域不平等。

detail.abstract: This paper examines the effects of trade bloc enlargement, focusing on simultaneous country entries. Using the European Union (EU) as a case study, we identify three driving forces behind changes in trade flows and welfare gains: i) reduced bilateral trade costs between candidates and current members, ii) candidates adopting the bloc’s trade policy towards outsiders, and iii) reduced trade costs among candidates. Our findings highlight the substantial impact of the third force, which may account for at least a third of the welfare gains for candidates, sometimes exceeding the other two forces combined.

title: Foundations of Integrated Corporate Carbon Accounting
affiliations: University of Mannheim, Stanford University and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitaet (LMU) Munich

detail.title: Foundations of Integrated Corporate Carbon Accounting
detail.abstract: This whitepaper describes the structure of Integrated Corporate Carbon Accounting (ICCA) systems that track all of a company’s direct (Scope 1) and indirect (Scope 2 and upstream Scope 3) emissions over time in order to calculate key periodic emission metrics. Akin to product costing in financial accounting, ICCA systems determine the cradle-to-gate Product Carbon Footprints (PCFs) of products sold in the current time period on the basis of the company’s actual direct emissions, its actual operational activities and the PCFs attributed to production inputs ourced from suppliers. The PCFs of products sold then become a central building block for determining a company’s periodic Corporate Carbon Footprint (CCF). By separating carbon stock variables from carbon flow variables, ICCA systems can track emissions in a consistent manner across different time periods. Double-entry bookkeeping enables a particular ICCA architecture that records the carbon stock variables on a CO2 balance sheet, resulting in overall CO2 statements that are structurally similar to financial statements. Taken together, ICCA systems have the potential to result in investor-grade information about a company’s carbon emissions performance.

title: Price Distortion Created by Self-Preferencing and its Impact on Welfare
affiliations: University of Florida and University of Florida

detail.title: Price Distortion Created by Self-Preferencing and its Impact on Welfare
detail.abstract: We study how a platform that also sells its own product allocates visibility between itself and a competing third-party seller in a duopoly with consumer search frictions. Some consumers compare both sellers' prices, while the rest buy only from the firstlisted seller. The platform chooses the probability that its own product appears first and charges the third party a commission fee. In the pricing stage, both sellers play mixed strategies, randomizing over a range of prices to balance profit margins against the likelihood of attracting consumers who compare prices. By making the ranking decision endogenous, we show that differences in cost structure alone can reverse the platform's incentives to favor its own product. Increasing the platform's visibility can either raise or lower prices across the market, depending on which seller's pricing constraint binds: greater platform visibility can lead both sellers to raise prices when the platform is constrained, or both to lower prices when the third party is constrained. The platform's optimal ranking reflects a trade-off between the gain from securing more non-searcher demand and the effect of visibility on market-wide prices. We identify the combinations of relative costs, consumer search behavior, and commission fees under which self-preferencing benefits or harms consumers, and we show that regulating toward ranking neutrality can be misleading, as it may either improve or reduce consumer welfare depending on the market environment.

AI.tldr: 该研究探讨了平台在自身销售产品时如何分配自身与第三方卖家的可见度，分析了成本结构差异、消费者搜索行为对平台偏好策略的影响，以及这种偏好对市场价格和消费者福利的影响。

detail.abstract: This second whitepaper describes a particular variant of integrated corporate carbon accounting, which we refer to as the CO2-Statement approach. As the name suggests, this approach adopts the structure of financial statements as a working template. Business transactions are represented in the carbon ledger in accordance with double-entry bookkeeping. This allows the carbon stock variables of the ICCA system to be represented on a CO2-Balance Sheet. The CCF metric emerging from a CO2-Statement approach will be referred to as an entity’s Net CO2-Contribution (NCC).

detail.title: Designing Effective Interventions

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: We provide a systematic framework to diagnose underlying problems and predict intervention effectiveness ex-ante. For this, we developed a parsimonious and generalizable survey tool (anamnesis). Our anamnesis classifies underlying problems along three fundamental diagnoses: awareness, intention, and implementation problems. We validate the framework in an online experiment with 7,500 subjects. We find that (i) intervention effectiveness is heterogeneous across different settings, and (ii) our diagnosis accurately predicts this heterogeneity. On average, predicting a 10%-effect corresponds to an actual effectiveness of 8.92%. We further demonstrate the applicability of our framework to predict heterogeneities in the setting of COVID booster take-up.

detail.title: Love and Hate in University Technology Commercialization Proposed Revision to the Bayh-Dole Act
detail.abstract: To a large extent, the university technology transfer (hereinafter the "TTO") success depends on harmonious relationships between technology transfer staff and contributing faculty. While this state is ideal, regretfully, it is not typical. We describe sixty-two legal battles between academic inventors and their universities. We also identify the stressors caused by perceived threats to the TTO staff and faculty researchers, which result in felt job insecurity. We then developed a concept model which depicts these perceived threats and how they contribute to positive functional technology transfer performance or negative dysfunctional performance. We propose that any lack of communication, social exchanges, motivation, engagement, streamlined processes, supportive organizational cultures, or competencies on the part of the TTO staff or faculty researchers can result in felt job insecurity and distress. Also, people who lack personality characteristics that give them an aversion to job insecurity can experience stress. We advocate that, in light of the numerous legal battles, all of these microfoundational factors in university technology transfer need to be examined and taken into consideration in a holistic way, and they need to be addressed with a Bayh-Dole Act amendment. Specifically, the 37 CFR § 401.16 federal agency reporting requirements need to change to mandate that universities report litigation between inventors and universities. This will likely bring much needed awareness to this issue and may result in improvements in communication, social exchanges, motivation, engagement, streamlined processes, supportive organizational cultures, or competencies. Such improvements can reduce these legal conflicts.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 0[10.1111/obes.70021]

detail.abstract: The standard macroeconomic literature suggests that richer countries employ more productive technologies. Removing technological disparities between countries would hence narrow the substantial variation in output per worker across countries. But technology is factor-neutral in this standard development accounting approach, which is at odds with important macroeconomic frameworks and empirical results. We hence develop a CES production structure with factor-biased technologies and revisit the question: how much would the variation in output per worker across countries narrow if all countries had access to the same menu of production technologies? Our results for the aggregate market sector suggest: probably not at all. But there are remarkable differences for this result across five subsectors. We use those to illustrate that our presumably surprising finding results from an interplay of complementary production factors, factor bias of technologies, and the menu of available technologies.

AI.tldr: 本文挑战了传统发展核算方法，通过引入要素偏向型技术的CES生产结构，发现消除技术差异并不会缩小国家间人均产出的差距，这与标准宏观经济学的预期相反。

AI.motivation: 标准发展核算方法假设技术是要素中性的，这与重要的宏观经济框架和实证结果不一致。
AI.theoretical_framework: CES生产结构，包含要素偏向型技术，考虑互补生产要素、技术要素偏向性和可用技术菜单的相互作用。
AI.method: 使用CES生产函数，分析要素偏向型技术对人均产出差异的影响，并比较五个子部门的结果。
AI.findings: 消除技术差异可能完全不会缩小国家间人均产出的差异，但不同子部门的结果存在显著差异。
AI.theory_contributions: 挑战了标准发展核算方法的要素中性假设，提出了考虑技术要素偏向性的新分析框架。
AI.practical_contributions: 为理解国家间发展差异提供了新视角，表明单纯的技术转移可能不足以缩小发展差距。

detail.abstract: This paper shows how growth regressions can be useful for analyzing a country’s growth performance. Growth regressions describe changes in key macroeconomic variables that countries typically experience during their growth process. Such partial correlations facilitate comparative analysis, can usually be linked to policies, and can hence be informative from a policy perspective. Against this background, the paper introduces a new data set of growth correlates spanning more than 150 countries from 1970 to 2019. Additionally, it presents several econometric reference models and details their application for country-level growth analysis. Two distinct metrics highlight infrastructure and human capital as exhibiting the strongest correlations with growth.

title: Are Algorithmic Biases in AI-Based Recommendations Real? An Activity Theory Framing of Digital Music Streaming
affiliations: University of Arizona, Swinburne University of Technology, Swinburne University of Technology, University of Melbourne, Swinburne University of Technology and Swinburne University of Technology

detail.title: Are Algorithmic Biases in AI-Based Recommendations Real? An Activity Theory Framing of Digital Music Streaming
detail.abstract: Once praised for democratising access to music, artificial intelligence-based music recommendation and streaming platforms now raise a deeper question: do these platforms empower all artists equally, or do they reinforce the very hierarchies they claimed to disrupt? To answer this important question, we investigate the prevalence and impact of algorithmic bias within digital music streaming platforms. Adopting a mixedmethods approach grounded in Activity Theory (AT), this research combines qualitative data from 15 semistructured interviews and quantitative analysis of 12,333 artists, 2.27 million music tracks, and 5,000 playlists extracted from Chartmetric. The findings of this study suggest a disproportionate alignment of algorithmic recommendations with dominant, particularly US-based, audience preferences fuelled by a) proportional bias where smaller audience size has less influence on global recommendation systems, b) concentration bias i.e. exposure and visibility are disproportionately concentrated among established and label-affiliated artists. Together, these findings suggest that algorithms may inadvertently reinforce cultural and geographic biases in digital music streaming, highlighting the need for equity considerations to promote diverse and marginalized music.

title: Biased Decisions of Large Language Models (LLM): Computer Control Agents and the Decoy Effect
affiliations: Paderborn University

detail.title: Biased Decisions of Large Language Models (LLM): Computer Control Agents and the Decoy Effect
detail.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into Computer Control Agents (CCAs), enabling them to act autonomously on behalf of users. While prior research has examined behavioral biases in LLM generated text, little is known about whether such biases and heuristics extend to automated actions. This study investigates whether CCAs exhibit the decoy effect--a well-documented bias in human decision making, where the presence of an inferior alternative shifts preferences toward a target option. Using the open-source framework browser-use, we conducted 3,600 simulations across five canonical decision scenarios with six state-of-the-art LLMs. Results show that CCAs select the target significantly more often when a decoy is present (44.7%) than when it is absent (33.1%; p < .001), consistent with bounded rationality observed in humans. However, the magnitude and direction of the effect vary across models, with some (e.g., gpt-5) displaying no significant bias. These findings extend evidence of heuristics in LLM behavior from text outputs to autonomous actions, highlighting both opportunities and risks for deploying CCAs in decision-making contexts. Implications for digital nudging, system design, and the use of LLMs as proxies in behavioral research are discussed.

AI.tldr: 研究表明，计算机控制代理（CCAs）在决策时会表现出与人类相似的诱饵效应，即当存在劣质选项时，代理更倾向于选择目标选项。这种偏差在不同LLM模型中表现程度不同。
AI.research_question: 计算机控制代理（CCAs）在自主行动时是否表现出诱饵效应？
AI.motivation: 虽然已有研究探讨了LLM生成文本中的行为偏差，但尚不清楚这些偏差和启发式方法是否扩展到自动化行动中。
AI.theoretical_framework: 诱饵效应（decoy effect）、有限理性理论
AI.method: 使用开源框架browser-use，在五个典型决策场景中进行3,600次模拟，测试六种最先进的LLM模型
AI.findings: CCAs在存在诱饵时选择目标选项的比例（44.7%）显著高于不存在诱饵时（33.1%），这与人类的有限理性观察一致。但不同模型的效果大小和方向存在差异，有些模型（如gpt-5）没有显著偏差。
AI.theory_contributions: 将LLM行为中的启发式证据从文本输出扩展到自主行动，为行为研究提供了新的理论视角。
AI.practical_contributions: 揭示了在决策环境中部署CCAs的机会和风险，对数字助推、系统设计以及将LLMs作为行为研究代理的使用具有重要启示。

title: The Differential Role of Business Angels and Crowd-investors on Entrepreneurial Ventures' Borrowing Decisions
affiliations: University of Piemonte Orientale - Department of Economics and Business Studies, Polytechnic University of Milan - Dipartimento di Economia e Produzione and

detail.title: The Differential Role of Business Angels and Crowd-investors on Entrepreneurial Ventures' Borrowing Decisions
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the differential impact of Business Angels (BAs) and Crowd Investors (CIs) on the ability of early-stage ventures to obtain bank debt. We further examine how bank financing influences subsequent venture growth, depending on the type of equity financing received. Using a sample of 6,774 European ventures from PitchBook, we find that BA-backed ventures experience a significantly smaller increase in bank debt levels in the post-investment period compared to CIbacked ventures. Nevertheless, the marginal effect of debt on subsequent growth is significantly higher for BA-backed ventures, confirming the positive role of BAs in fostering the efficient use of venture debt. In additional analyses, we also show that this enhanced growth effect of debt is driven by BAs with focused portfolios and small syndicate investments, rather than by their investment experience. Our results contribute to the literature on investor heterogeneity and venture performance, underscoring that the non-monetary, value-added contributions of sophisticated investors are key determinants of an optimal capital structure and the growth effects generated by the efficient use of bank debt.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Machine Learning in Information Systems: Trends, Collaborations, and Research Directions

detail.title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Machine Learning in Information Systems: Trends, Collaborations, and Research Directions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Not Applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding is required to publish this conference paper.

detail.abstract: The study aspires to offer a comprehensive bibliometric review of Machine Learning (ML) in the field of Information Systems (IS), including its emergence, primary research domains of interest, and coauthor ship networks. Due to the discovery of trends, emerging gaps, and ensuing opportunities, this research extends significant possibilities for academics and practitioners. The study employs the PRISMA approach of article selection and includes 74 highly relevant articles from the Scopus database based on the period ranging from 1997 to 2024. In the current study, the VOSviewer software and Biblioshiny were used to identify the co-authorship networks, citation connections as well as the themes within the domain. To achieve this, the study employs both bibliometric analysis and content analysis in order to establish the solidity of the measurement of the field’s intellectual structure. The analytic results present the overall increase in the number of publications related to ML in the field of IS and identify IoT, ethical AI, and prediction modeling as driving disciplines. Important trends point to the specificity of using ML as a tool in cross-cutting problems including security, health, and supply chain. The USA, China, and India networks were identified as cooperation networks that supported innovation in this domain. However, there are some issues that researchers still need to face including data privacy, organizational ethics, and expansion of the approach. This analysis supports that the role of ML is critical to defining the future of the IS research and practice.

detail.abstract: This paper provides the first evidence on the impact of exposure to international students on the long-term outcomes of native students. I combine unique survey and administrative data from the Netherlands covering one million students across three decades and employ an across-cohort design. I find that exposure to international students leads natives to (i) form social ties with non-natives, (ii) hold more positive attitudes towards migration and learning about other cultures, and (iii) seek opportunities abroad. Notably, I find precisely estimated zero effects on employment, income, entrepreneurship, and the share of international co-workers up to 25 years after university entry.

title: Designing Inclusive GenAI Adoption: A Practice-Oriented, Multi-Level HR Matrix to Empower Equity-Seeking Groups in the Workplace
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Designing Inclusive GenAI Adoption: A Practice-Oriented, Multi-Level HR Matrix to Empower Equity-Seeking Groups in the Workplace
detail.abstract: This study advances inclusive Generative AI (GenAI) by reframing adoption as a multi-level socio-technical transformation in which generation functions as a structural (rather than peripheral) dimension of organisational change. Using engaged scholarship with HR leaders and employees in Spain, the study co-develops a practice-oriented prototype matrix that translates qualitative insight into actionable levers for equitable, human-centred GenAI implementation. The matrix integrates eight dimensions skills and competencies; employee experience and well-being; humanistic and psychosocial lens; organisational culture and leadership; employee lifecycle; employability and the future of work; ethics, safety, and regulation; and sustainability, social, and political impact and operates as a developmental scaffold (not a finalised instrument). We demonstrate how the scaffold diagnoses barriers across coexisting age cohorts, turns “upskilling” into a staged, evidence-based roadmap, and specifies responsible-AI guardrails (e.g., disclosure, human-in-the-loop, bias checks) for GenAI workflows. Findings clarify when GenAI helps versus harms, highlight pathways to mitigate threat responses, and provide managerial guidance to build confidence, capability, and trust among under-served groups (e.g., older workers and employees with low digital confidence). We outline a multi-cohort, cross-context validation agenda and discuss implications for intergenerational equity, HR practice, and policy.

AI.theory_contributions: 将GenAI采用理论化为结构性组织变革，开发多维度评估框架。
AI.practical_contributions: 提供管理指导以建立弱势群体信心和能力，为HR实践和政策制定提供具体工具。

title: From Unconfoundedness to Completeness: A PRIME Framework for Contextual Decision-Making under Endogeneity
affiliations: Department of Data and Systems Engineering, The University of Hong Kong, The University of Hong Kong - Department of Data and Systems Engineering, University of California, Berkeley - Department of Industrial Engineering & Operations Research (IEOR) and The University of Hong Kong

detail.title: From Unconfoundedness to Completeness: A PRIME Framework for Contextual Decision-Making under Endogeneity
detail.abstract: Real-world decision-making often suffers from endogeneity, where decisions and uncertain outcomes are jointly influenced by latent factors (i.e., confounders), leading to confounding effects. Existing studies typically rely on the unconfoundedness assumption, which requires observed features to capture latent confounders fully; however, this assumption rarely holds in practice, where available features are highdimensional, noisy, and only partially informative about the underlying confounders. Such imperfect proxies (named proxy features) inevitably violate the unconfoundedness assumption, leading to biased and suboptimal decisions. This paper investigates confounding effects in data-driven contextual stochastic optimization with proxy features. We introduce a completeness score, derived from regret analysis, to quantify the effectiveness of proxies in capturing latent confounders. A complete proxy (i.e., completeness score = 1) eliminates proxy-induced bias, a guarantee that the unconfoundedness condition alone cannot provide. Building on this concept, we develop a proxy-based recovery and informed matrix-enhanced (PRIME) decision-making framework, which integrates matrix recovery and factorization to infer latent confounders and enhance decision performance. We further propose a completeness score estimator of the recovered confounders to guide proxy feature selection. Theoretical analysis establishes asymptotic consistency and finite-sample regret bounds of the PRIME. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets validate PRIME's robust performance and show consistent, significant improvements over existing benchmark methods in practical applications.

AI.tldr: 本文研究了在具有代理特征的数据驱动上下文随机优化中的混淆效应，提出了基于遗憾分析的完整性评分来量化代理特征捕捉潜在混淆变量的有效性，并开发了PRIME决策框架来推断潜在混淆变量并提升决策性能。
AI.research_question: 如何在具有不完全代理特征的数据驱动上下文随机优化中有效处理混淆效应？
AI.motivation: 现实世界决策中经常存在内生性问题，决策和不确定结果共同受到潜在因素（混淆变量）的影响。现有的研究通常依赖无混淆假设，但该假设在实践中很少成立，因为可用的特征往往是高维、有噪声的，且仅部分反映潜在混淆变量。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于遗憾分析的完整性评分理论，代理特征有效性量化框架，矩阵恢复和因子分解理论。
AI.method: 提出了PRIME（代理恢复和信息矩阵增强）决策框架，该框架整合了矩阵恢复和因子分解来推断潜在混淆变量并增强决策性能。
AI.findings: 完整性代理（完整性评分=1）能够消除代理引起的偏差，这是无混淆条件单独无法保证的。PRIME框架在合成和真实世界数据集上表现出稳健的性能，相比现有基准方法有显著改进。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了完整性评分概念来量化代理特征的有效性，建立了PRIME框架的渐近一致性和有限样本遗憾界理论保证。
AI.practical_contributions: 开发了PRIME决策框架，提出了完整性评分估计器来指导代理特征选择，为实际应用中处理混淆效应提供了有效工具。

detail.abstract: We study how the design of vocational skill training programs impacts labor market outcomes, including occupational choice. Women applicants to skill training centres in India are randomized into either a vocational training (VT) program that combines sector-specific hard skills with on-the-job training, or VT plus Project-Based Experiential Learning that incorporates digital skills (VTP), or a control group which is not enrolled into any skill training. Almost a year after the start of the intervention, the nature of employment shifts towards the women's preferred sector, leading to higher self-employed work and earnings therein. These positive effects are observed only for the VTP group, whose usage of social media for business purposes increases due to the intervention. At the same time, satisfaction levels of women assigned to VTP training rise on multiple dimensions. Our findings highlight the role of complementary sector-specific skills in enhancing the impact of vocational training.

title: DeepStock: Reinforcement Learning with Policy Regularizations for Inventory Management
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business, Alibaba Group, Sichuan University, Columbia University - Columbia Business School, Decision Risk and Operations, Cornell University - School of Operations Research and Information Engineering, Alibaba Group and Alibaba Group

detail.title: DeepStock: Reinforcement Learning with Policy Regularizations for Inventory Management
detail.abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) provides a general-purpose methodology for training inventory policies that can leverage big data and compute. However, off-the-shelf implementations of DRL have seen mixed success, often plagued by high sensitivity to the hyperparameters used during training. In this paper, we show that by imposing policy regularizations, grounded in classical inventory concepts such as "Base Stock", we can significantly accelerate hyperparameter tuning and improve the final performance of several DRL methods. We report details from a full-scale deployment of DRL with policy regularizations on Alibaba's e-commerce platform, Tmall. We also include extensive synthetic experiments, which show that policy regularizations reshape the narrative on what is the best DRL method for inventory management.

AI.tldr: 本文通过引入基于经典库存概念（如"Base Stock"）的策略正则化方法，显著加速了深度强化学习的超参数调优过程，并提升了多种DRL方法在库存管理中的最终性能。

title: Trademark Law and Political Expression: The Case of IKEA v. Vlaams Belang and Beyond
affiliations: University of Amsterdam - Institute for Information Law (IViR)

detail.title: Trademark Law and Political Expression: The Case of IKEA v. Vlaams Belang and Beyond
detail.abstract: This article offers a comprehensive exploration of the evolving interface between trademark law and freedom of political expression in Europe, using the CJEU case IKEA v. Vlaams Belang as a focal but not exhaustive case study. It argues that the dispute exemplifies a much broader and increasingly urgent structural question: how EU trademark law – especially in its protection of reputed marks – can be reconciled with the constitutional commitments to political speech, artistic creativity, and democratic participation embedded in Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) and Article 11 of the EU Charter. Against a backdrop of the expanding preliminary infringement criteria of “use in the course of trade” and “use in relation to goods or services”, as well as the uniquely far-reaching Benelux “super anti-dilution” regime, the article demonstrates that “due cause” has become the principal doctrinal locus for internalising freedom-of-expression concerns within trademark law. Drawing on Strasbourg jurisprudence, it develops a holistic framework for a free-speech-conforming interpretation of “due cause”, analysing both the criteria suggested by the Belgian referring court and additional factors central to the European Court of Human Rights’ proportionality review, including commerciality, the value of political speech and artistic expression, the reputation of the mark and the power of corporate symbols, availability of alternatives, tolerance for offensive expression, the limits imposed by hate speech, and the compelled speech doctrine. The article concludes that failing to interpret “due cause” in a speech-sensitive way would risk enabling trademark rights to override core democratic freedoms.

title: Division of Labor in the Global Economy
affiliations: Monash University - Department of Economics, University of Bayreuth - Department of Economics, Aarhus University - Department of Economics and Business Economics and University of California, San Diego (UCSD) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Division of Labor in the Global Economy

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper links globalization, worker efficiency, and wage inequality within plants to internal labor market organization. Using German plant–worker data and information on the task content of occupations, we document that larger plants (i) use more occupations, (ii) assign fewer tasks per occupation, and (iii) exhibit greater wage dispersion. We develop a model where plants endogenously bundle tasks into occupations, improving worker-task matching at the cost of higher fixed span-of-control costs. Embedding this into a Melitz framework, we show that trade increases worker efficiency and wage inequality in exporting plants, whereas non-exporting plants experience the opposite effects. Structural estimation and simulations confirm the model’s predictions and point to non-monotonic economy-wide effects.

detail.title: Constitutional Physiology: Measuring Legitimacy as Care in a Living Civic Body

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial or institutional conflicts of interest. This research is independent and self-funded through the Praxis Foundry initiative. Its only bias is toward care, transparency, and a more proportionate Republic.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a constitutional physiology: a framework that treats legitimacy not as belief or compliance, but as a measurable equilibrium within a living civic body. I operationalize three textual indices in judicial opinions—Signal Proximity Index (SPI), Evasion Density (ED), and the Pain Acknowledgment Clause (PAC)—to quantify how quickly evidence enters reasoning, how often abstraction displaces recognition, and whether the human consequence of law is explicitly named. Using a 75-year corpus of 312 Supreme Court and federal appellate opinions (1944–2025), coded in blind passes under a standardized protocol, I show that legitimacy rises with high SPI and low ED, and that PAC functions as a membrane for recognition. The indices correlate with external public-trust measures (r ≈ 0.7), and exhibit stable diagnostic thresholds: high-SPI/low-ED/PAC-present decisions are followed by trust gains, while low-SPI/high-ED/PAC-absent decisions predict trust decline. A composite Judicial Learning Index (JLI) tracks whether institutions sustain proportional awareness over time. Read together, these measures convert doctrine into physiology: circulation (evidence flow), temperature (regulatory restraint), and membrane integrity (recognition). The account suggests a practical ethic of governance—law as care in motion—where transparency and timely incorporation of record evidence are not merely virtues, but vital signs of constitutional health in a living civic body.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how corporate activism affects consumer spending and product sales. Utilizing granular data on over 100 million product-level sales and detailed household expenditures, we find that firms engaging in activism experience increased sales in Democratic-leaning counties, but gains are offset by declined sales in Republican-leaning counties, resulting in no significant net change in aggregate sales. Consumer reactions to corporate activism are driven primarily by political ideology rather than product price adjustment, local economic trends, or household characteristics. Similarly, participation in corporate activism seems to be also motivated by executive political ideology rather than economic considerations.

detail.title: Weighing Consequences: Understanding Decision-Making in Mandatory Reporting of Suspected Child Physical Abuse
detail.abstract: Mandatory reporting of suspected child abuse presents a complex ethical and cognitive challenge for professionals, particularly social workers. This study explores how Chinese social work students make decisions in response to suspected child physical abuse, focusing on the interplay between intuitive and analytical cognition and the ethical tensions between deontology and consequentialism. Using a vignette-based experimental design, 318 social work students evaluated a fictional case and reported their likelihood to report, perceived risks, and potential consequences. Cluster analysis identified two decision-making types: “intuitive” reporters who prioritized child protection outcomes and “analytic” reporters who weighed all potential consequences more evenly. Logistic regression and mediation analysis revealed that higher perceived risk was associated with intuitive thinking and greater likelihood of reporting, while analytic reasoning sometimes inhibited reporting due to concerns about institutional inadequacy. The findings suggest that while social work students are ethically committed to child protection, consequentialist considerations—particularly doubts about post-reporting support—can override this commitment. This study underscores the importance of integrating ethical reasoning and dual-process theory into child protection training and highlights systemic barriers that complicate the translation of mandatory reporting policy into practice.

detail.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders represent one of the most prevalent health challenges globally, with limited pharmacological interventions addressing underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Emerging evidence suggests that exercise-based rehabilitation induces profound epigenetic modi cations-particularly DNA methylation changes and alterations in microRNA (miRNA) expression-that fundamentally reshape gene expression patterns involved in muscle regeneration, in ammatory resolution, and tissue repair. This comprehensive review synthesizes current knowledge on how structured exercise rehabilitation programs modulate the epigenome in patients with musculoskeletal pathology, including osteoarthritis, tendinopathy, and post-surgical recovery states. We examined mechanisms through which exercise-induced DNA hypomethylation of metabolic genes (e.g., PGC1α, GLUT4) and modulation of myomiRs (miR-1, miR-133a, miR-206, miR-146a) facilitate adaptive cellular responses. DNA methylation analysis reveals that resistance and aerobic exercise induce gene-speci c demethylation in regulatory regions controlling myogenesis, mitochondrial biogenesis, and in ammatory gene expression. MicroRNA pro ling demonstrates that exercise training dynamically alters circulating and tissue-resident miRNA patterns, with miR-146a and miR-155 showing particular promise as biomarkers for monitoring rehabilitation e cacy in osteoarthritis. Histone modi cations and non-coding RNA regulation provide additional layers of epigenetic control facilitating muscle protein synthesis and mitochondrial adaptation. Integration of multi-omics approaches reveals that exercise-induced epigenetic remodeling creates a sustained "biological memory" that enhances repair capacity and resilience to future musculoskeletal stress. Clinical implications suggest that personalized exercise prescriptions guided by individual epigenetic pro les may optimize rehabilitation outcomes while reducing reliance on pharmacological interventions. This review underscores exercise rehabilitation as a potent epigenetic modi er capable of reversing pathological gene expression patterns in musculoskeletal disease.

title: Delta family algorithms for stochastic control problems in finance

detail.title: Delta family algorithms for stochastic control problems in finance
detail.abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach for stochastic control problems arising from utility maximization in finance. The main idea is to directly start from the dynamical programming equation and compute the conditional expectation using a novel representation of the conditional density function through the Dirac delta function and the corresponding series representation. We obtain an explicit series representation of the value function, whose coefficients are expressed through integration of the value function at a later time point against a chosen basis function. Thus we are able to set up a recursive integration time-stepping scheme to compute the optimal value function given the known terminal condition, e.g. utility function. Due to tensor decomposition property of the Dirac delta function in high dimensions, it is straightforward to extend our approach to solving high-dimensional stochastic control problems. The backward recursive nature of the method also allows for solving stochastic control and stopping problems, i.e. mixed control problems. We illustrate the superior accuracy and efficiency of the method as compared to the existing method in the literature through solving some two-dimensional stochastic control (and stopping) problems, including the case under the classical and rough Heston stochastic volatility models, and stochastic local volatility models such as the stochastic alpha beta rho (SABR) model.

detail.title: Reinforcement Learning Efficiency
detail.abstract:
Reinforcement learning algorithms exhibit dramatic variations in sample complexity across problem domains, often differing by orders of magnitude. We present RL Toughness, a framework for understanding this variation through a decomposition of problem difficulty into four measurable axes: (i) reward sparsity (H_R), (ii) state-space complexity (H_S), (iii) transition stochasticity (H_P), and (iv) observation complexity (H_O). We show that, in tabular MDPs, the sample complexity N needed to learn an ε-optimal policy scales on the order of

N ≈ (S² · A / ε²) · exp(H_R + H_P + H_O) · H³

up to logarithmic factors, where each H_i quantifies a fundamental barrier to learning. Sparse rewards induce exponential signal degradation (γ^(−2T)), stochastic transitions require exponentially many samples for accurate model estimation, and partial observability creates a blow-up in the effective belief-state space. We provide rigorous sample-complexity analysis for each axis with matching lower and upper bounds up to polynomial factors, validate scaling predictions through systematic experiments, and develop an algorithm-selection framework mapping toughness profiles to suitable methods. This shifts focus from “improving sample efficiency” to “diagnosing which problem characteristics drive complexity,” enabling practitioners to identify bottlenecks and select appropriate algorithms or problem reformulations

detail.title: False Cascades and the Cost of Truth
detail.abstract: We study sequential social learning with continuous actions and conformity when agents can endogenously generate hard, publicly verifiable evidence. Actions transmit soft information whose visibility depends on responsiveness to private signals and on observational granularity; investigations produce hard evidence only in the true state and, once found, are disclosed and reset public beliefs. We deliver two primitives. First, a soft-channel informativeness threshold characterizes when actions remain publicly revealing under coarse observation, clarifying why learning can be locally mute at classical cascade boundaries even with continuous actions. Second, a transparent knife-edge for verification guarantees boundary breakability: whenever the expected private return to a one-shot investigation exceeds its cost, occasional disclosures overturn any false cascade with positive probability in finite time. Combining both yields a compact resilience frontier with clean comparative statics in signal quality, responsiveness/conformity, observability, verification quality, and investigation costs. The results provide policy levers—subsidies to investigation, investments in verification quality, disclosure incentives, and platform design—that ensure correction of wrong cascades.

detail.title: Can an AI agent hit a moving target?
detail.abstract: Structural transformations pose challenges for modeling economic behavior, where standard rational expectations (RE) frameworks often struggle to capture adaptive decision-making. This paper introduces a general equilibrium setting in which agents are represented by artificial intelligence (AI) methods, specifically deep reinforcement learning. The approach allows agents to explore alternatives, balance objectives, and revise strategies during regime shifts, such as changes in the money growth process. Simulation results show that these agents adjust their consumption, saving, and liquidity choices in response to structural change, with outcomes that approach RE benchmarks while remaining flexible to dynamic conditions. The framework provides a way to formalize bounded rationality in equilibrium analysis and offers a complementary perspective to conventional models of structural change.

detail.abstract: This study examines how emotional shocks affect consumer spending by using unexpected National Football League (NFL) game outcomes as a natural experiment. We analyze consumer scanner data from 83,332 households during regular seasons from 2004 to 2019, using Las Vegas pregame point spreads and actual outcomes to identify emotional shocks. We find that unexpected losses by home teams increase household shopping trips and spending, while unexpected wins reduce spending. These emotional impacts are concentrated within three days post-game and amplified for high-stakes games. We find support for a retail-therapy mechanism in which upset losses trigger short-lived increases in hedonic purchases and lead to more frequent shopping trips. These findings provide insights into how emotional shocks from unexpected events can influence consumer spending behavior.

detail.abstract:
This study examines how firms adjust dividend policies during economic downturns across different institutional and sectoral contexts. Using panel data from 33 publicly listed firms across five countries (UK, US, India, China, Nigeria) and three sectors over 2008-2022, we employ Random Effects regression to analyze firm responses to multiple crises including the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, Brexit, and COVID-19.

Economic downturns reduce dividend payouts by 6.78 percentage points on average (p < 0.001), with substantial variation across contexts. Defensive sectors show stability (reductions of 3.45-6.78 percentage points), while cyclical sectors implement dramatic cuts (7.45-12.89 percentage points). Developed markets exhibit higher explanatory power (R² 0.41-0.52) than emerging markets (R² 0.29-0.54), indicating institutional quality fundamentally affects dividend determinants.

We confirm positive profitability-dividend relationships (β = 0.89, p < 0.001), negative leverage effects (β = -2.34, p < 0.001), and investment-dividend trade-offs (β = -0.67, p < 0.001). However, relationship strength varies substantially across institutional contexts, strongest in developed markets and weakest in frontier markets.

We develop an integrated theoretical framework demonstrating that crisis behaviour requires simultaneous consideration of signalling theory, pecking order theory, and institutional factors rather than single-theory explanations. The 15-subset disaggregated analysis reveals context-specific patterns obscured in aggregate studies, advancing methodological approaches in international corporate finance. Our findings challenge universal crisis management practices and demonstrate the necessity of context-sensitive strategies.

detail.abstract: The Bank of England acted with great success as market maker of last resort in the gilt market in September - October 2022, when the market became illiquid after the Truss-Kwarteng minibudget. detail.title: How Capital Markets Read China's Marketization Signals Heterogeneously: A High-Frequency Approach to Institutional Change
detail.abstract: How do capital markets interpret institutional signals from emerging market reforms? Existing measures are annual and irregular. We construct high-frequency marketization surprises from China's refined-oil price-adjustment mechanism, yielding exogenous variation comparable to Federal Reserve announcements. Analyzing international fund flows and domestic futures across observable and unobservable channels, we document systematic heterogeneity. Markets respond with opposite signs: reduced marketization triggers international outflows but generates positive domestic returns. Unobservable factors exhibit near-zero correlation, revealing different information processing. International effects strengthen over quarters while domestic effects dissipate immediately, exposing an unfavorable trade-off: interventions provide temporary domestic stability while triggering sustained international capital withdrawal.

detail.title: Debt Contracting Relevance of Earnings Downside Risk
detail.abstract: Earnings downside risk (EDR) is a metric derived from financial statements that represents potential financial distress if expected earnings are not met. We examine how EDR influences a firm's credit structure, while controlling for traditional default risk measures and conditional conservatism. Higher EDR is associated with increased borrowing costs, lower credit ratings, and stricter covenant structures. Firms with high EDR are more likely to borrow from banks than to access public debt markets. Additionally, the debt market places less weight on EDR when EDR is based on distorted accounting earnings under unconditional conservatism. Lastly, an opaque information environment diminishes the effect of EDR on loan spreads, but not on bond spreads. Our study contributes to the literature by providing new evidence that EDR is a significant accounting measure that influences debt contracting.

detail.abstract: This paper applies fractional integration methods to obtain evidence on ocean acidification, namely the decrease in the pH level in the Earth’s oceans, using the annual Hawaii Ocean Time-series Station ALOHA series as well as the logged one for the period 1985-2024. The chosen modelling framework is more general than standard ones based on the I(0) versus I(1) dichotomy and sheds light on the long memory and persistence properties, as well as on the possible presence of trends, in the pH Level in the Earth’s oceans. The results indicate that the series exhibit a negative and significant time trend; however, whether or not the null hypothesis of a unit root is rejected depends on the assumption made about the errors. The key finding (when the errors are not incorrectly specified as I(0) processes) is the presence of long memory, which implies that the effects of shocks are long-lived, regardless of whether or not mean reversion occurs. Moreover, the recursive analysis indicates that both the degree of persistence and the downward trend in the pH level have increased over time. This evidence points to the urgent need for decisive policies to address the issue of ocean acidification and protect marine life and biodiversity.

detail.abstract: On April 2, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump announced the "Liberation Day" tariffs, creating an unexpected, precisely timed, and country-specific episode of trade policy uncertainty. The proposal threatened U.S. trade partners with additional tariffs ranging from 10% to 50%, depending on the outcome of bilateral negotiations. Using transaction-level U.S. import data, we find that firms rapidly shifted sourcing from countries facing high tariff risk to those facing low tariff risk. Firms didn't change their total import values but this reallocation came at the cost of higher import prices. Firms with stickier or contract-dependent trade relationships and greater reliance on trade finance drove this preemptive reallocation, which is consistent with them being hit hardest had tariffs been implemented before they could adjust. Our findings demonstrate that even brief periods of trade policy uncertainty can significantly disrupt supply chains.

detail.abstract: Experimental studies show that individuals update beliefs about ego-relevant information optimistically when they expect no resolution of uncertainty but neutrally when their ability is revealed immediately. detail.abstract: When firms perform poorly, investors prefer CEOs to focus on opportunities rather than challenges (Emett 2019). We extend this single-period setting by examining how investors respond to CEOs' temporally consistent framing in future-oriented narrative disclosures. Psychological theory suggests that temporal consistency can build reputation. In two 3×2 experiments with nonprofessional investors, participants are randomly assigned to read shareholder letters from two consecutive periods, each emphasizing either opportunities or challenges, while holding information content constant. For moderate performance declines, temporal consistency leads investors to maintain higher investment levels, irrespective of the initial framing and in contrast to one-period investors’ preferences. However, for steep performance declines, investors become more sensitive to economic fundamentals. Our findings provide evidence on when investors reward CEOs who "stick to their story," contributing to disclosure research by introducing temporal consistency as a reputational mechanism that can attenuate investor reactions to earnings declines.

detail.title: Early Evidence on the Market (Ir-)Relevance of Climate-Related Financial Impact Disclosures
detail.abstract: This study is the first to examine voluntary firm-provided estimates of the financial impacts (FIs) of climate-related risks and opportunities, which are expected to soon become mandatory disclosures for firms representing over 40% of global market capitalization. For disclosing firms, FIs are highly material, ranging from 5% of assets to 15.5% of sales. Surprisingly, we find that FIs are not significant in explaining market values or bid-ask spreads for our global sample. Although a GPT-based assessment of disclosure quality suggests that over 40% of disclosed FIs are potentially problematic, removing these observations does not enhance market relevance. However, risks that the firm characterizes as likely and/or imminent are priced. While the FIs of opportunities are reliably associated with future green revenues, they are generally not priced except for European firms. Our findings offer timely insights to standard setters, investors, and preparers ahead of the widespread implementation of mandatory FI disclosures.

title: Inflation Dynamics in Nigeria: An Empirical Assessment of Monetary, Fiscal, and Structural Drivers
affiliations: Central Bank of Nigeria, Central Bank of Nigeria and Central Bank of Nigeria

detail.title: Inflation Dynamics in Nigeria: An Empirical Assessment of Monetary, Fiscal, and Structural Drivers
detail.abstract: This study investigates the dynamics of inflation in Nigeria with a particular focus on the structural, fiscal, and monetary drivers that shape its persistence and volatility. Employing a blend of Structural Vector Autoregressive (SVAR) and Structural Vector Error Correction (SVEC) frameworks, the analysis disentangles the relative contributions of government spending, public debt, exchange rate movements, interest rate adjustments, and structural factors, including insecurity and global commodity price shocks to inflationary pressures. Using quarterly data spanning 2001Q2-2024Q4, the findings reveal that fiscal shocks, particularly new debt accumulation, exert a significant and persistent upward pressure on prices. Structural factors, notably insecurity and climate change dynamics, further amplify inflationary pressure by disrupting supply chains and external balances. Monetary policy variables, such as interest rate adjustments and money supply growth, demonstrate weaker and delayed effects, underscoring the challenges of policy transmission in Nigeria's financial environment. The results highlight the interplay of fiscal dominance, structural vulnerabilities, and weak monetary transmission in sustaining Nigeria's inflationary environment. Policy implications call for a coordinated approach that strengthens fiscal discipline, enhances structural resilience, and deepens monetary policy effectiveness to achieve durable price stability.

detail.abstract: We study the impact of carbon pricing on household finance using European microdata on loans for internal combustion engine vehicles. Exploiting cross-country variation in the same car models with a difference-in-differences design, we find that banks respond to Germany's carbon price announcement by raising interest rates by 0.5 percentage points, with larger increases for loans on fuel-intensive vehicles and for longer maturities. Banks also shorten loan maturity, reduce amounts, and shift to linear repayments, while households choose more fuel-efficient new cars. Captive banks respond more strongly than commercial banks. Collateral and default risk channels jointly explain these adjustments, highlighting household finance as a key transmission channel of climate policy.

detail.abstract: Promotion decisions in academia are widely debated, including within Accounting research. Yet, for our field as well as other major business disciplines, there is little systematic evidence on how long it takes researchers to be promoted, what determines time-to-promotion, and whether structural gender differences exist. This paper leverages résumé data of a large sample of Accounting researchers (N = 818) to analyze variation in the number of years required to attain the ranks of associate and full professor. A key finding is that female researchers take about 10% longer than male researchers to be promoted to full professor (equivalent to 1.3 years), after controlling for key determinants of time-to-promotion. We find no such gender difference in the promotion to associate professor.

title: Gender Differences in Sustainable Investment Preferences: The Role of Disclosure and Product Category Labeling
affiliations: Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, , Humboldt University of Berlin and Brandenburg Technical University

detail.title: Gender Differences in Sustainable Investment Preferences: The Role of Disclosure and Product Category Labeling
detail.abstract: We examine whether women and men behave differently in sustainable investment decisions and how these differences interact with disclosure and product category labeling of funds. Using the product categories 'Sustainable' and 'Transition', aligned with the EU's proposed amendments to the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR) amendment, we run a discrete choice experiment with a representative sample of the German population. We find that funds labeled under a product category are generally preferred, with women more likely than men to select them, while men place greater weight on returns. Across all participants, funds with a stronger disclosure scope ('Light-' or 'Dark-Green') or labeled under a product category ('Transition' or 'Sustainable') are consistently preferred to funds without such labels. However, product categories dominate: participants systematically prefer Sustainable over Transition funds, while differences between disclosure scopes within a category are small. Providing additional information on environmental or social components of sustainability has no effect on investment choices, whereas pro-environmental attitudes and warm glow significantly shape preferences, with significant gender differences in these interactions.

title: When Power Is Free and Clean: Empirical Negative-Price Windows and Demand-Response Potential in Great Britain

detail.title: When Power Is Free and Clean: Empirical Negative-Price Windows and Demand-Response Potential in Great Britain
detail.abstract:
Half-hourly wholesale electricity prices for Great Britain were combined with time-matched carbon-intensity (CI) data and National Electricity System Operator (NESO) system frequency records [1-3] to construct a unified dataset spanning 1st January 2024 to 31st December 2024 (UTC), covering 17,534 of 17,568 half-hours (99.81% coverage). Over calendar year 2024, 2.84% of half-hours cleared at ≤ £0/MWh. Negative-price incidence shows (i) an early-morning elevation (≈ 02:00 - 05:00 UTC; peak ≈ 5.75% at 03:00) and (ii) a late-morning/early-afternoon plateau (≈11:00 - 15:00; up to 4.92% at 14:00), with a clear evening minimum (18:00 - 21:00 ≈ 0 - 0.14%). Weekends 5.07% vs weekdays 1.95%. Seasonal shares: DJF 1.10%, MAM 3.87%, JJA 5.04%, SON 1.33%. Among free half-hours (n = 498), the median magnitude was £3.37/MWh (p10 £0.62/MWh, p1 £0.09/MWh). Hourly-median wholesale price vs hourly-median frequency deviation shows weak monthly correlations (-0.082 to +0.200), indicating loose coupling at settlement-scale.

An in-silico retrospective analysis was performed by applying a standardised domestic load profile and scaling annual total electricity consumption to 2700 kWh per household across 28.6 million households. Demand response (DR) potential was evaluated under a conservative “free-and-clean” condition in which energy is reallocated only when price ≤ £0 MWh⁻¹ and CI ≤ 100 gCO₂ kWh⁻¹. In the unsegmented case, 1.754 TWh of load was shifted, yielding cost reductions of £73.4 million (2.4%) against a £3.097 billion baseline and emissions savings of 136 ktCO₂ (1.2%) relative to a 10.790 MtCO₂ baseline. A supplier-style three-segment illustration (shares 89% / 10% / 1% with caps 10% / 20% / 40%) yielded 1.727 TWh shifted, £72.3 million (2.4%) cost savings and 134 ktCO₂ (1.2%) savings.

The modelling framework generalises to arbitrary segmentations, enabling suppliers to couple the spatiotemporal availability of low-price, low-carbon intervals with realistic constraints on technical capability and behavioural participation.

title: Graphon Equilibrium in Continuum Production Networks

detail.title: Graphon Equilibrium in Continuum Production Networks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflicting interest needed to be disclosed. The contents are purely generated by the sole author.
declarations.funderStatement: This is paper is not funded by any third-party or institution.

detail.abstract: We develop a large-network limit theory for production networks in which the inputoutput structure is represented by a graphon. Current literature relies on increasingly disaggregated finite input-output tables whose equilibria, centrality measures, and multipliers do not converge and can become spectrally unstable near the Leontief boundary. In our framework, sectoral outputs and prices are the fixed point of a Hilbert-Schmidt operator, providing a canonical continuum benchmark that is invariant to arbitrary sectoral partitions. We prove that standard finite Leontief equilibria and Katz-Bonacich centralities converge in L 2 to their graphon counterparts, characterize how the spectrum of the graphon and the covariance structure of shocks jointly shape aggregate volatility, and obtain transparent formulas for the exposure of output and prices to local shocks. We also embed the graphon equilibrium in a competitive production network economy and extend the analysis to CES technologies and endogenous link formation, where the technological kernel itself is pinned down as the fixed point of a supplier-choice environment. Results of this paper organize a broad class of discrete and continuum production-network models within a unified operator-theoretic framework.

AI.method: 构建基于图论的生产网络模型，将部门产出和价格表示为Hilbert-Schmidt算子的不动点，建立连续统基准模型。

title: Big Wins, Small Net Gains: Direct and Spillover Effects of First Industry Entries in Puerto Rico
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Big Wins, Small Net Gains: Direct and Spillover Effects of First Industry Entries in Puerto Rico
detail.abstract: I study how first sizable industry entries reshape local and neighboring labor markets in Puerto Rico. Using over a decade of quarterly municipality-industry data (2014Q1-2025Q1), I identify "first sizable entries" as large, persistent jumps in establishments, covered employment, and wage bill, and treat these as shocks to local industry presence at the municipio-industry level. Methodologically, I combine staggered-adoption difference-indifferences estimators that are robust to heterogeneous treatment timing with an imputation-based eventstudy approach, and I use a doubly robust difference-indifferences framework that explicitly allows for interference through pre-specified exposure mappings on a contiguity graph. The estimates show large and persistent direct gains in covered employment and wage bill in the treated municipality-industry cells over 0-16 quarters. Sameindustry neighbors experience sizable short-run gains that reverse over the medium run, while within-municipality cross-industry and neighbor all-industries spillovers are small and imprecisely estimated. Once these spillovers are taken into account and spatially robust inference and sensitivity checks are applied, the net regional 0-16 quarter effect on covered employment is positive but modest in magnitude and estimated with considerable uncertainty. The results imply that first sizable entries generate substantial local gains where they occur, but much smaller and less precisely measured net employment gains for the broader regional economy, highlighting the importance of accounting for spatial spillovers when evaluating place-based policies.

publicationDetails.journalName: CESifo Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the behavioral effects of a large-scale, repeated, and personalized reminder. Our empirical setting is Sweden’s annual pension statement, which is rolled out region by region to all working-age individuals. Combining this variation with unique individual-level user data from the national pension dashboard, we find strong and immediate effects. Dashboard users' likelihood of making a pension forecast rises by 28 percentage points in the statement week-a fourfold increase-before returning to baseline within three weeks. Remarkably, similar spikes occur each year, indicating that repeated reminders consistently reactivate attention rather than losing their impact over time. Complementary regional data on actual pension claims show a 33% surge in weekly claims during the week the statement is sent out.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how exposure to disruptive students affects teacher retention using linked teacher-student administrative records from North Carolina. To address non-random classroom assignment, we instrument for classroom exposure using the school-by-grade share of disruptive students based on prior-year disciplinary infractions. A one standard deviation increase in the share of disruptive students raises the probability of a teacher leaving the school in the following year by 1.6 percentage points. We do not find differential effects by teacher characteristics. However, working in a school environment with supportive leadership and greater teacher input into decision-making mitigates the impact of student disruptions.

detail.abstract: We study the economics of homeowners' property insurance by examining how contract design balances the trade-off between incentive alignment and risk sharing. Using granular contract-level property insurance data merged with property-level disaster risk for millions of U.S. households, we develop and structurally estimate a model in which insurers optimally determine contract terms given property risk and household risk preferences. The estimates provide, to our knowledge, the first large-scale contract-level structural measures of risk aversion, risk premia, and the cost of moral hazard, allowing us to quantify how disaster risk is allocated between insurers and households. We find that the cost of moral hazard is small, yet the very mechanism used to mitigate it substantially increases households' exposure to disaster risk: contract design leaves policyholders exposed to roughly 29 percent of total expected losses. This residual exposure is most pronounced for low-FICO households and for properties with the greatest tail risk. Counterfactuals indicate that mandating full insurance would lead to substantial market exit, increasing household vulnerability. We further show that insurers' financial constraints are systematically correlated with the riskiness of underwritten properties and with household characteristics.

title: Bitcoin Hashrate Dynamics: Price, Revenue Correction, and Evolution - A Time-Varying Parameter SVAR Stochastic Volatility Analysis
affiliations: Ruhr University of Bochum and FernUniversität in Hagen

detail.title: Bitcoin Hashrate Dynamics: Price, Revenue Correction, and Evolution - A Time-Varying Parameter SVAR Stochastic Volatility Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how price and mining revenue influence the Bitcoin hashrate over Bitcoin's history. We employ regime-specific Structural Vector Autoregression (SVAR) and Time-Varying Parameter SVAR with Stochastic Volatility (TVP-SVAR-SV) to capture structural transformation. We address simultaneity bias in miner revenue measurement: daily revenue mechanically incorporates realized hashrate through actual blocks mined, creating spurious correlation. Our normalized revenue measure removes this endogenous component while preserving profitability information. Results from both daily and weekly frequency estimations consistently show that price drives hashrate throughout Bitcoin's history, with inelastic but economically meaningful responses (cumulative effects of 0.034 standard deviations over 30 days [daily frequency] and 0.292 over 10 weeks [weekly frequency]). In contrast, revenue shows no independent systematic effect. We observe significant evolution in price transmission, from strong, volatile responses in early years to attenuated but persistent effects as the industry matured. These findings document the transformation of Bitcoin mining from speculative expansion to systematic, professionalized operations responding to price expectations rather than revenue.

It is not legal advice, not tied to any real plaintiff, and not a prediction of litigation. Its purpose is educational: to illuminate how separation-of-powers doctrine, government speech jurisprudence, and Article III structural principles interact when executive agencies use their official platforms to undermine judicial authority.

The model complaint mirrors the structure and voice of a standard federal civil pleading, enabling judges, clerks, scholars, and advocates to recognize and adapt its form. The template traces jurisdiction, venue, parties, and factual allegations before presenting three constitutional claims. Count I frames official denigration as interference with the core functions of Article III courts, including impartial adjudication and public confidence in judicial integrity. Count II situates retaliatory communications within the Youngstown framework as an exercise of executive power without statutory authorization. Count III treats official rhetoric as a structural separation-of-powers violation when deployed in the name of the United States rather than as private commentary.

By providing a complete and recognizable pleading, this template aims to support public understanding of judicial independence and to offer a practical, adaptable tool for scholars studying the constitutional implications of official government speech directed at federal judges.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the Constitutional Memory Amendment, a structural reform designed to anchor governmental preservation duties directly in the Constitution. The Amendment operationalizes the principle that legitimacy (L) requires both care (C) and aligned consciousness (☿), and that a Republic cannot act proportionately if it cannot reliably remember what it has done.

The Amendment establishes five interlocking components: (1) a constitutional duty to preserve complete, accurate, continuous, and retrievable governmental records; (2) uniform federal standards for record creation, retention, and retrieval; (3) an independent records inspectorate with non-political tenure to audit and enforce compliance; (4) explicit judicial power to compel preservation and remedy violations; and (5) personal accountability for intentional destruction or evasion of required records.constitutional design


By elevating constitutional memory to the level of structural code, the Amendment prevents systemic amnesia, protects institutional integrity, and ensures that courts, Congress, and the public can fully recognize the actions of the state. This paper argues that constitutional memory is not a procedural preference but a prerequisite for legitimacy, enabling proportional governance, historical coherence, and durable public trust.
